findings.title: Startup rollback frees a resource while the spawned child is still live
findings.summary: JobExecutor attaches a spawned process handle before creating and starting the sole child-exit waiter. A waiter-installation exception propagates to StartJobProcessor, whose catch frees the retained allocation without checking whether a child already owns it. The resource manager immediately returns the unit to its free deque. This exposes available capacity while the child may still use its launch binding, without an installed waiter owning normal cleanup.
findings.dedup_note: also covers code-review Scenario 2 (same post-spawn startup rollback and cleanup-ownership mechanism)

findings.title: A stale deployment write can undo an acknowledged pre-run abort
findings.summary: JobRunner checks SUBMITTED before deployment, then writes DISPATCHED unconditionally. The concurrent pre-run abort handler reads status once, stores ABORTED, and constructs a success response from its saved branch. Deployment can overwrite that terminal value before the response is constructed. The built-in job manager performs a plain metadata update without an expected-state condition.
findings.dedup_note: also covers code-review Scenario 3 (same stale pre-run status decision and unguarded status-write mechanism)

findings.title: A delayed startup write can restore RUNNING after terminal publication
findings.summary: JobRunner publishes running_jobs membership under its lock, then stores RUNNING after releasing that lock. The completion thread can observe the entry after server exit and outcome resolution and publish a terminal status first. The delayed startup write then restores RUNNING. Completion can subsequently delete its bookkeeping without another status publication.
findings.dedup_note: also covers code-review Scenario 3 (same non-atomic RUNNING and terminal status publication mechanism)

findings.title: Allocation identity crosses shared process environment
findings.scenario: Scenario 1: Allocation identity crosses shared process environment
findings.summary: Scenario 1 hypothesizes that a job-local allocation is written into the process-global CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES environment before the launcher snapshots the environment for a child process. A delayed legitimate START can overlap a later admitted job, allowing another consume step to update the shared parent environment between allocation and snapshot. The resulting child launch binding could diverge from the resource manager's reservation and allocation ownership even when tokens and allocations are distinct. Recorded Scenario 1 model-checking runs were bounded and reported no violation, so this remains a code-review candidate without a counterexample.

findings.title: Logical termination, outcome receipt and physical cleanup diverge
findings.scenario: Scenario 4: Logical termination, outcome receipt and physical cleanup diverge
findings.summary: Scenario 4 hypothesizes that logical termination, terminal outcome receipt, scheduler membership, and physical resource cleanup can be driven by different observations on separate control loops. The client side normally keeps resource ownership until the child-process waiter observes exit and reaches free_resources, while server abort and completion paths can update bookkeeping from command or outcome state. Delayed outcome reporting, archival, heartbeat, or terminate handling could therefore matter for duplicate release, early release, or omitted release. Recorded Scenario 4 model-checking runs were bounded and reported no violation, so this remains a code-review candidate without a counterexample.

findings.title: Per-job failure can escape a scheduling or completion service
findings.scenario: Scenario 5: Per-job failure can escape a scheduling or completion service
findings.summary: Scenario 5 hypothesizes that a per-job failure can escape or damage scheduling and completion service state because error containment differs across the admission pass, runner startup failure branch, startup cleanup, and completion retries. The scheduler catches exceptions around a candidate pass, while the runner failure branch performs removal, stop, status, metadata, and event work inside one exception path. Completion publication and map deletion can also overlap startup-failure removal paths, so retry accounting and later eligible-job progress depend on service survival and cleanup ownership. Recorded Scenario 5 model-checking runs were bounded and reported no violation, so this remains a code-review candidate without a counterexample.
